messages:
Alex M: Heads-up — after yesterday's burst test we saw p95 sitting fine but p99 spikes across the board during scale-up windows. Looks correlated with cold KV misses and kernel fallback churn. Posting profiler snippet below.
Jordan P: Can you paste the flame/trace? quick numbers are enough.
Alex M: Sure. From the 60s burst window: p50=22ms p95=120ms p99=420ms; cpu-steal/timeouts negligible. KV hit-rate on first tokens ~28% then climbs to 86% after ~8s. Kernel selector logged ~12 fallbacks from avx2->scalar for short seqs.
Maria S: Oof. That KV warmup curve matches the scale-up lag. Did we try aggressive prefix caching for the hot routes? We saw good gains in canary.
Alex M: We had prefix caching enabled, but autoscaler brought up fresh workers with empty caches. Those workers also picked a different kernel due to model-threading heuristics, which cost us ~50–80ms on cold requests.
Jordan P: Snip of profiler (trimmed):
```
[trace id=tr-9b13]
kernel_select: 1.9ms
kv_lookup: 6.2ms (miss 72%)
microbatch_wait: 14ms
infer_core(avx): 18ms
infer_fallback(scalar): 72ms
KV_populate: 42ms
```
That's per-request instrumentation inside a scaled-up node.
DevEx: Repro steps? Which workload / batching policy did you run?
Alex M: Synthetic chat burst: 600 rps for 45s, model = rwkv-7b-like, microbatch target = 16, max_wait_ms = 12. Autoscaler policy: aggressive add-on 2 nodes at 60s threshold. Node bring-up ~6–9s including readiness probes.
Maria S: Two related knobs: 1) microbatch target + max_wait_ms — smaller targets reduce head-of-line for cold requests, 2) kernel pinning for early requests so we avoid fallback thrash.
Jordan P: Suggestion: add warm-pool capacity to handle short bursts (keeps KV warm) and have new nodes start in a low-traffic probe mode which only accept a small fraction of traffic until KV warmed.
Alex M: Agreed. Also thinking about a quick heuristic: if node_start_time < 20s then force quantized/fast kernel choice consistent with other nodes (avoid selector variance) and disable complex matmul paths.
SRE Bot: Incident 2026-03-16T21:07: autoscale-induced p99 > SLO on /generate for 4m. Pager noted. :warning:
Maria S: We should also tweak p99 alert thresholds to ignore short windows when autoscaler in progress. But we must not hide real regressions.
Jordan P: Can we run an A/B with two microbatch configs (8 vs 16) under the same burst to see tail sensitivity? I'll spin a canary.
DevEx: I can add a quick dashboard: compare node_age, kv_hit_rate, kernel_variant, p95/p99. Useful to see correlation live.
Alex M: Action items:
- Jordan run AB burst with microbatch 8 vs 16 and capture traces (J:ETA 2h)
- DevEx add dashboard panels for node_age & kernel_variant (ETA 1h)
- Maria prototype startup probe that funnels <5% traffic until kv_hit_rate>60% (ETA EOD)
- Ops explore warm-pool config + cost estimate (ETA tomorrow)
Jordan P: Starting the canary now, ping when traces land. @Maria S want to join the trace triage?
Maria S: Yep, joining in 15.
Alex M: Thanks all. If canary shows microbatch 8 reduces p99 we may ship a temporary policy to lower default for bursty endpoints.
Jordan P: Early canary numbers: p95 ~110ms both; p99 320ms (mb=16) vs 190ms (mb=8) during first 20s. Promising.
DevEx: Dashboard posted: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/rtl-1779002468 (link)
Alex M: Nice work — we'll iterate. Keeping this thread for follow-ups.
